title: Delta Significance Heatmap: Bakeoff Summary and Decision Memo
content:
Purpose:
This memo summarizes the June 2027 delta-significance heatmap bakeoff run across three candidate model versions (v4.2-small, v4.2-medium, v4.3-quant) against the current serving baseline (v4.1). The goal was to surface statistically meaningful wins and losses across a dense promptset matrix, identify brittle prompt cohorts, and produce a single recommended candidate for staged rollout to canary traffic.

High-level decision: 
- Recommendation: promote v4.2-medium to canary (10% traffic) for two weeks with active quality monitoring. v4.3-quant shows cost promise but has significant degradation on instruction-following and numeric reasoning cohorts. v4.2-small wins latency and cost but loses on coherence for long-context prompts.

Why this run (context):
- Prior A/Bs (May 2027) flagged small but noisy gains in token-efficiency for 4.3 quantized variants. Teams requested a deeper sweep that measures significance over many prompt cohorts and computes a clustered heatmap of wins/losses with p-value thresholds. This run was intended to:
  1) quantify significance (bootstrap CIs + paired t-tests) rather than point estimates,
  2) expose cohort-specific regressions (long-context, tables, instruction-follow, code), and
  3) produce a compact decision signal for PM/Eng.

Dataset / promptsets used:
- Base evaluation corpus: 18k prompts sampled from production shadow traffic (stratified by endpoint: chat, completion, rerank).
- Seeded edge cohorts (1.8k prompts total):
  - long-context (>2048 tokens) 600 prompts
  - numeric reasoning 400 prompts
  - instruction-following (multi-step) 400 prompts
  - code generation small functions 200 prompts
  - table extraction 200 prompts
- Prompt pre-processing: normalized whitespace, removed personally identifiable snippets, replaced timestamps with placeholders.
- Evaluation harness: deterministic sampling where applicable (temp=0.2), 3 seeds for non-deterministic ops.

Metrics and statistical tests:
- Primary metrics: quality_score (0-100 human-calibrated surrogate from eval rubric), factuality_f1, instruction_adherence_pct, latency_p50_ms, tokens_per_response, cost_per_request_usd.
- Statistical method: paired bootstrap (10k resamples) for 95% CI, paired t-test for p-values. We flag deltas as: 
  - Significant win: delta > 2.5 points on quality_score and p < 0.01 or CI excludes 0.
  - Mild win/loss: delta 0.5-2.5 points with p < 0.05.
  - Significant loss: delta < -2.5 points and p < 0.01.
- Heatmap construction: prompt cohorts along rows, metrics along columns, cell value = ranked z-score of delta (baseline -> candidate). Cells annotated with stars for significance.

Summary leaderboard (aggregate, weighted quality_score across cohorts):
- v4.2-medium: 68.4 (baseline 64.2)  +4.2 overall (significant)
- v4.1 (baseline): 64.2
- v4.2-small: 62.0  -2.2 (mild loss on long-context/coherence)
- v4.3-quant: 59.8  -4.4 (significant loss on instruction-follow and numeric reasoning)

Win / loss overview (counts across 20 cohort x metric checks):
- v4.2-medium: wins 12, neutral 5, losses 3
- v4.2-small: wins 6, neutral 6, losses 8
- v4.3-quant: wins 4, neutral 5, losses 11

Selected cohort callouts (deltas and significance):
- Long-context (>2048):
  - v4.2-medium: -1.0 quality (p=0.12) mild degradation, but within CI
  - v4.2-small: -3.6 quality (p=0.004) significant loss; coherence and hallucination incidence up 6%
  - v4.3-quant: -5.2 quality (p<0.001) significant loss; broken KV cache behavior in quant path observed in traces
- Numeric reasoning:
  - v4.2-medium: +1.8 quality (p=0.03) mild gain
  - v4.3-quant: -4.8 quality (p<0.001) significant loss; arithmetic error rate +9 pp
- Instruction-following (multi-step):
  - v4.2-medium: +3.5 (p=0.005) significant win on step decomposition
  - v4.2-small: -1.4 (p=0.09) not significant
  - v4.3-quant: -6.1 (p<0.001) large loss; prompt truncation artifacts detected in sample outputs
- Table extraction:
  - v4.2-medium: +0.6 (p=0.18) neutral
  - v4.3-quant: -1.0 (p=0.07) mild loss

Latency and cost tradeoffs:
- v4.2-small: median latency p50 down 18% vs baseline, cost/request -22% (wins on infra economics).
- v4.2-medium: latency p50 down 6%, cost/request -8% — good balance of cost and quality.
- v4.3-quant: latency p50 down 12%, cost/request -35% but quality dropouts in key cohorts make it risky for general rollout.

Failure modes and traces (engineering notes):
- v4.3-quant showed KV cache misalignment for long sequences. Trace IDs attached in linked artifacts; reproducible in local repro harness when sequence window crosses quant packing boundary.
- v4.2-small shows increased token repetition on multi-paragraph completions; hypothesized reason is shorter attention head capacity leading to looped generation in the top-k sampling cluster.

Heatmap examples (excerpts):
- Row: numeric reasoning | columns: quality_delta = -4.8 (v4.3-quant) [***], instruction_adherence = -6.2 [***], latency = -12% [n.s.].
- Row: instruction-following | v4.2-medium quality_delta +3.5 [**], v4.3-quant quality_delta -6.1 [***].

Decision rationale (why v4.2-medium to canary):
1) Statistically significant net quality gain across priority cohorts (instruction-follow and numeric reasoning).
2) Modest cost improvements without risky regressions in long-context or table tasks.
3) Engineering traces for v4.2-medium show no KV cache breakage; rollout risk is low.
4) Will allow collection of live signal for hallucination/factuality with small user impact window.

Canary rollout plan (if approved):
- Week 0: Deploy v4.2-medium to canary bucket (10% of production traffic split by customer tier to minimize enterprise impact). Enable full logging, sample outputs retention 1:10, auto-alerts on quality_score drop >=2.0 vs baseline in any priority cohort.
- Week 1: Review daily dashboard; if any significant negative drift in instruction-follow or numeric reasoning (>=2 confirmed deltas), pause rollout and revert.
- Week 2: If stable, expand to 30% for 1 week then evaluate for full rollout.

Monitoring and gating metrics (auto):
- daily aggregated quality_score delta (rolling 24h) per cohort; threshold -1.5 triggers page to applied-ml-oncall.
- latency p95 increase >15% triggers infra-runbook.
- hallucination rate increase >2.0 pp triggers emergency review.

Open questions / follow-ups before full rollout:
- Can engineering reproduce v4.3-quant KV misalignment in an isolated e2e test (action assigned to @Ethan Li, ticket REDW-1298)?
- Do we need a targeted instruction-follow shadow test on high-value enterprise routes (product to schedule)? (action: PMs to nominate 50 enterprise prompts)
- Investigate whether further quantization with per-layer fallback would recover v4.3-quant quality while preserving cost.

Appendix A: raw win/loss table snapshot (simplified)
- Format: cohort | v4.2-medium (delta, p) | v4.2-small (delta, p) | v4.3-quant (delta, p)
- long-context | -1.0 (0.12) | -3.6 (0.004)*** | -5.2 (<0.001)***
- numeric-reasoning | +1.8 (0.03)* | -0.8 (0.32) | -4.8 (<0.001)***
- instruction-follow | +3.5 (0.005)** | -1.4 (0.09) | -6.1 (<0.001)***
- table-extraction | +0.6 (0.18) | -0.4 (0.26) | -1.0 (0.07)

Appendix B: reproducibility notes
- Seeds and harness config: repo: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-harness commit 7a9c1f2, seed list attached in linked artifact.
- Evaluation machine mix: 4xA100 for candidate scoring, local dev repro with 2xA10 for KV trace reproduction.

Summary for PM / Eng leadership (TL;DR):
- v4.2-medium: better quality where it matters, modest cost wins -> recommended canary.
- v4.2-small: cheaper and faster but loses coherence on long-context -> keep as cost-optimized variant but not default.
- v4.3-quant: impressive cost savings, but unacceptable quality regressions on critical cohorts -> hold and investigate locked quant fallback.

Next steps (owners):
- Approve canary for v4.2-medium (owner: Priya)
- Investigate v4.3-quant KV misalignment (owner: Ethan) - REDW-1298
- Prepare enterprise shadow route for instruction-follow cohort (owner: Marco)

Notes: this doc is a working decision memo; please add comments and tag people for follow-ups.
